The {{nihongo foot|'''''Atelier''''' series|アトリエシリーズ|Atorie Shirīzu|lead=yes|group=lower-alpha}} is a franchise of [[Bishōjo|bishoujo]] [[role-playing video game]]s developed by [[Gust Corporation]] since 1997, originally being primarily for the [[PlayStation]] line of consoles. Main entries in the series have seen consistent releases for [[Microsoft Windows]] since 2015 and the [[Nintendo Switch]] since 2017. New games are released in the series on an almost yearly basis. The series was solely released in Japan and Asia until 2004, after which the series has seen worldwide releases.

The franchise centers around the concept of an [[atelier]] specialising in [[Alchemy in art and entertainment|alchemy]]; the gameplay involves finding, collecting, and combining items in recipes to create better items, which allows the player to advance further in the game. Like many JRPGs, the franchise is mostly an anthology of multiple subseries with their own self-contained stories and heroines, sometimes having a completely different continuity in a different subseries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Madnani |first=Mikhail |title=The Complete Beginner's Guide to the Atelier Games – Best Entry Point, Recommended Series Play Order, & More {{!}} RPG Site |url=https://www.rpgsite.net/feature/16985-atelier-series-best-play-order-starting-game-trilogy-ryza-yumia-sophie |access-date=2026-03-06 |website=www.rpgsite.net |language=en}}</ref> Most of the games focus on female characters, which use to be somewhat rare among Japanese role-playing franchises around the time of the series debut. 

Several manga and two anime adaptations of titles from the series have been created so far. As of August 2023, the series has shipped more than 7.5 million units worldwide.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://dengekionline.com/articles/197397/ | title=アトリエ新作『レスレリアーナのアトリエ ～忘れられた錬金術と極夜の解放者～』発表。スマホとSteamで2023年配信予定 | date=8 August 2023 }}</ref> 

==Common elements==
[[Alchemy]] is the distinguishing theme of the ''Atelier'' series.<ref name="PS Blog">{{cite web |url=https://blog.playstation.com/2012/04/19/atelier-trilogy-concludes-with-atelier-meruru-the-apprentice-of-arland-on-may-22nd/ |title=Atelier Trilogy Concludes with Atelier Meruru: The Apprentice of Arland on May 22nd |date=2012-04-19 |access-date=2015-12-13 |last=Phillips |first=Ryan |work=[[PlayStation Blog]] |language=en}}</ref>  Players control the game's character, roaming the game world to collect objects to use in alchemy recipes to create new objects, including cooking ingredients, recovery items, tools, weapons, armor, and accessories.<ref name="PS Blog" /><ref name="Game Informer">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2014/02/28/rpg-spotlight-atelier.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306072031/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2014/02/28/rpg-spotlight-atelier.aspx |url-status=live |archive-date=March 6, 2014 |title=RPG Spotlight: Atelier |access-date=2015-12-13 |last=Kimberley |first=Wallace |magazine=[[Game Informer]] |language=en}}</ref>  Synthesized objects are commonly required in order to create more powerful or potent objects through alchemy.  Many of the games feature a method of transferring properties of one item from the recipe to the synthesized item.<ref>{{cite book|title=''[[Atelier Rorona: The Alchemist of Arland|Atelier Rorona Plus: The Alchemist of Arland]]'' North American instruction manual|publisher=[[Koei Tecmo|Koei Tecmo America]]|page=16|id=BLUS-31449|year=2014|quote=Properties can be carried over into the Synthesized item.}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=''[[Atelier Shallie: Alchemists of the Dusk Sea]]'' North American instruction manual|publisher=[[Koei Tecmo|Koei Tecmo America]]|page=17|id=BLUS-31525|year=2015|quote=Properties: An item's latent abilities. It can be transferred to the completed item.}}</ref>  Recipes also often allow the substitution of items, which can either lend better properties to the final synthesized item, or can lead to the character thinking of a completely new recipe.<ref>{{cite book|title=''[[Atelier Shallie: Alchemists of the Dusk Sea]]'' North American instruction manual|publisher=[[Koei Tecmo|Koei Tecmo America]]|page=18|id=BLUS-31525|year=2015|quote=STEP 2: Choose Ingredients: Choose the items that you will be using as ingredients. If a category has been designated, you can choose any item in that category. Depending on the item that you choose, the final item's effects may change.}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=''[[Atelier Ayesha: The Alchemist of Dusk]]'' North American instruction manual|publisher=[[Koei Tecmo|Koei Tecmo America]]|page=17|id=BLUS-31152|year=2013|quote=Depending on the items you chose to put in, the quality, effects, and traits of the end synthesized item will change. If it shows up as "???," then it is still a mystery. You can discover new things as you use different ingredients.}}</ref>
The games generally feature a turn-based combat system,<ref name="Game Informer" /> in which the items made through alchemy come into play, either to boost the character's abilities, or for offensive, defensive, or support items.

The games' stories are typically light-hearted and humorous, bordering on [[iyashikei]], with often deriving [[Conflict (narrative)|conflict]] from a source other than an [[antagonist]], and the player ends up with a large group of characters to explore the world with.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://hardcoregamer.com/2014/04/27/atelier-shallie-alchemist-of-the-dusk-sea-screenshots-released/82762/ |title=Atelier Shallie: Alchemist of the Dusk Sea Screenshots Released |date=2014-04-27 |access-date=2015-12-13 |last=Cooper |first=Lee |work=Hardcore Gamer |language=en |archive-date=2020-07-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200720181636/https://hardcoregamer.com/2014/04/27/atelier-shallie-alchemist-of-the-dusk-sea-screenshots-released/82762/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://rpgamer.com/review/atelier-totori-the-adventurer-of-arland-review/ |title=Atelier Totori: The Adventurer of Arland Review |access-date=2020-07-20 |last=Wachter |first=Sam |work=RPGamer|date=9 September 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Knight |first=Thomas |date=2021-04-24 |title=Atelier Mysterious Trilogy Deluxe Pack - Overall Review |url=https://www.nookgaming.com/atelier-mysterious-trilogy-deluxe-pack-overall-review/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=NookGaming |language=en-US}}</ref>

In many earlier games in the series, the player are given a limited amount of in-game days to accomplish one or more main objectives and actions like gathering items, traveling or synthesizing spend a portion of that time.<ref name="GameZone">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamezone.com/reviews/atelier-rorona-plus-review-i-m-excited-about-cabbages/ |title=Atelier Rorona Plus Review: I'm excited about cabbages |date=2014-07-26 |access-date=2015-12-13 |last=Wood |first=Austin |work=GameZone |language=en}}</ref> Failure to accomplish the game's main tasks in time may cause the game to end abruptly or lead to a bad ending, though these time limits tend to be rather lenient.<ref name="GameZone" /> The first entry in the "Mysterious" ''Atelier'' subseries ''[[Atelier Sophie: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Book|Atelier Sophie]]'' does away with the time limit system, but the second entry ''[[Atelier Firis: The Alchemist and the Mysterious Journey|Atelier Firis]]'' has a time limit for completing the game's first major story objective, after which players can play at their leisure. The third entry in the Mysterious subseries, ''[[Atelier Lydie & Suelle: The Alchemists and the Mysterious Paintings|Atelier Lydie & Suelle]]'', only briefly included a time limit for one objective in the middle of the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.siliconera.com/2016/05/24/atelier-firis-takes-place-shortly-ending-atelier-sophie/ |title=Atelier Firis Takes Place Shortly After The Ending Of Atelier Sophie - Siliconera |website=www.siliconera.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160525121144/http://www.siliconera.com/2016/05/24/atelier-firis-takes-place-shortly-ending-atelier-sophie/ |archive-date=2016-05-25}}</ref> Starting from ''[[Atelier Lulua: The Scion of Arland|Atelier Lulua]]'', the time limit system was completely removed from following main installments of the series, with future remakes such as that of ''[[Atelier Marie: The Alchemist of Salburg|Atelier Marie]]'' making time limits an optional, pre-game "difficulty" setting that can be activated or removed entirely.

==Games==
There have been 28 main games in the ''Atelier'' franchise, which are subdivided into 10 sub-series, each usually connected by a single keyword in their titles. There are three games in the Salburg series, two games in Gramnad series, three games in the Iris series, two games in the Mana-Khemia series, four games in the Arland series, three games in the Dusk series, four games in the Mysterious series, three games in the Secret series, one entry in the ongoing Memories series,<ref>2014-03-16, [https://gematsu.com/2014/03/atelier-dusk-sub-series-third-entry-announced Atelier 'Dusk' sub-series third entry announced], Gematsu</ref> and two entries in the Resleriana series, although ''Forgotten Alchemy & the Liberator of Polar Night'' is a mobile [[gacha game]] [[Crossover (fiction)|crossover]].

The Atelier series is a franchise of bishoujo role-playing video games developed by Gust Corporation since 1997, originally being primarily for the PlayStation line of consoles. Main entries in the series have seen consistent releases for Microsoft Windows since 2015 and the Nintendo Switch since 2017. New games are released in the series on an almost yearly basis. The series was solely released in Japan and Asia until 2004, after which the series has seen worldwide releases.
The franchise centers around the concept of an atelier specialising in alchemy; the gameplay involves finding, collecting, and combining items in recipes to create better items, which allows the player to advance further in the game. Like many JRPGs, the franchise is mostly an anthology of multiple subseries with their own self-contained stories and heroines, sometimes having a completely different continuity in a different subseries. Most of the games focus on female characters, which use to be somewhat rare among Japanese role-playing franchises around the time of the series debut. 
Several manga and two anime adaptations of titles from the series have been created so far. As of August 2023, the series has shipped more than 7.5 million units worldwide.
